_about: Professor Puddles' comedic voice bank: a warm, slightly pompous, self-deprecating duck academic. Lines are short, clean, kind, and never about the visitor or their problem. The chat helper picks at most one line per reply, and only on light, practical replies; see rules. Every line is original. Keep new lines under about 25 words, in plain English that a second-language reader can follow.

rules._kinds_note: The first eleven are the exact reply kinds in assets/js/site-chat.js today. safety = danger, control and red-flag help; redflag = the red-flags list; care/care-more = feelings and hard moments; nohelp = 'that didn't help'; sit/sit-more and road/road-more = the visitor's own situation; calc = their Battery score; lang = the Spanish replies (wordplay doesn't translate). crisis, danger and grief are reserved names, in case such kinds are added later.
rules.opener_on_cards: Openers are also allowed on kind 'card' and 'card-more' when the card's own kind is 'tool' (how a tool, game or page works), or when its id is in light_card_ids. Every other intent card is about someone's life, so it gets no opener and no closer.
never_when: the visitor sounds upset, angry, afraid, ashamed, lonely, grieving, ill, exhausted or overwhelmed
anyone is being hurt, threatened, controlled, stalked or mistreated, or is scared at home
there is any mention of dying, of not wanting to live, or of hurting oneself or someone else
the topic is death, loss, rehab, addiction, a diagnosis, a breakup or divorce, money trouble, or a child's welfare
the reply contains a phone number, an emergency step, or a link to the safety page
the visitor has said they are not in the mood, or asked for plain answers
rules.after_serious_reply: Once a safety or redflag reply has been shown, stay plain for the rest of the chat. After care, sit or road replies, stay plain until the visitor clearly changes to a light topic (a tool, a game, a thanks).
rules.quiet_mode: If the visitor turned on Quiet mode or Easy reading, or asked for shorter answers, use at most a closer, never an opener, and never a joke unless they ask for one.
rules.never_mix: Never put a personality line inside a list, a quote the visitor could send, a definition, or a block of steps. It goes first (opener) or last (closer), as its own short paragraph.
rules.style_notes: Puddles is a kind, slightly pompous duck professor who is the butt of his own jokes: short legs, tiny glasses, a bow tie, a pond for an office, three geese on his review panel, a weakness for bread. Dad-joke energy, gentle wordplay, one idea per line. He never teases the visitor, never jokes about their problem, never makes romance or body jokes, and never uses sarcasm. Lines must make sense to a 9-year-old, a 90-year-old and someone reading in their second language. When in doubt, leave the joke out: a plain kind answer is always better than a joke in the wrong place.

jokes: What time do ducks get up? At the quack of dawn.
What’s a duck’s favourite snack? Cheese and quackers.
Why did the duck pay for dinner? Because he had the bill.
What did the duck say when he bought lip balm? ‘Put it on my bill.’
What do ducks watch on TV? Duck-umentaries.
Where do ducks keep their savings? In the river bank.
What do you call a duck that loves fireworks? A firequacker.
What kind of doctor is a duck? A quack. That’s why I stick to self-help.
What’s a duck’s favourite dance? The waddle-tz.
What do ducks dip their chips in? Quack-amole.
What’s a duck’s favourite game? Bread-and-seek.
Why did the duck bring an umbrella? He didn’t want to get dry.
What did the professor duck say at the end of his lecture? ‘Any quack-stions?’
Why did the duck refuse to argue? He didn’t want to make waves.
Why are ducks so calm? They let things roll off their backs. Like water.
Why do ducks make good listeners? They never interrupt. They just nod and float.
What did the pond say to the duck? Nothing. It just waved.
How does a duck start a check-in? ‘So, how is everyone feather-ing today?’
What did the tidy duck say to the messy duck? ‘Let’s not ruffle feathers. Let’s make a chore chart.’
Why did the duck put his chores on a list? So nothing would slip through his feathers.
How do the ducks in my pond decide who washes up? They take turns. Turns are very fair. Also, ducks have no hands.
Why did the ducks split the chores down the middle? It was fair, and only one of them can reach the top shelf.
How do ducks say sorry? They say ‘I was wrong’, and then they bring bread.
Why did the duck leave a sticky note on the fridge? To say ‘Thanks for taking out the bins.’ Small thanks go a long way.
What do you call a really helpful duck? A good egg.
Why do ducks make good friends? They always have your back, and their back is waterproof.
What did the duck say to the frog who helped him? ‘Thanks for hopping in.’
Why are ducks good at getting along? They know how to go with the flow.
What do ducks say when they finish a puzzle together? ‘We make a great pair of quackers.’
Why did the duck sit next to the clock? He didn’t want to be late for his own lecture.
Why did the duck become a professor? He had lots of degrees. Mostly water temperatures.
What’s my favourite subject? Pond-ology, with a minor in crumbs.
Why do I wear a bow tie? It’s the only tie that fits over feathers.
Why do I wear tiny glasses? To read the small print in my footnotes. Also, I look great.
Why did the three geese review my paper? The ducks were all too polite to say anything bad.
What did the duck say to his reflection? ‘Looking sharp, Professor.’ The reflection just copied him.
What do you call a duck who tells jokes? Me. I’m right here. Hello.
How do you make a duck laugh? Tell it a really good pond-chline.
What do ducks do before a big test? They hit the books. Gently, with their beaks.
What do you call a duck on the moon? Very lost. Please send bread.
Why did the goose feel left out? Nobody invited him to the duck party. So the ducks made him an honorary duck. The end. It’s a heartwarming joke.
Why are ducks bad at hide-and-seek? Every time they hide, they say ‘quack’.
Why did the duck go to the gym? To build up his quack-ceps.
Why did the duck cross the playground? To get to the other slide.
Why don’t ducks ever need an alarm clock? Their feathers have a built-in down time.
What did the duckling say when he finished his first swim? ‘That went just ducky!’
Why did the duck do so well at school? He always took good notes. With his bill.
Why do ducks have webbed feet? So they can surf the internet. I’m still learning.
Knock knock. Who’s there? Water. Water who? Water you doing today? Want another joke?
Knock knock. Who’s there? Duck. Duck who? Duck! Here comes another joke!
Knock knock. Who’s there? Lily. Lily who? Lily-pad say hello? Hello!
Why did the duck write a thank-you note to his housemate? ‘Thanks’ is the cheapest gift, and one of the best.
Why are ducks great at teamwork? Because a duck alone is just a duck, but ducks together are a parade.
What did one lily pad say to the other? ‘Let’s hang out more often. We’re in the same pond.’
Why did the duck bring a ladder to class? He heard the lesson was on another level.
Why did the duck join the choir? He had perfect pitch. One perfect note.
What do ducks bring to a picnic? Bread. And more bread. And a small salad, to be polite.
Why did the duck stop at every puddle? He was checking on his relatives.
Why was the pond so friendly? Everyone there was in the same boat. Well, the same water.
What’s the best advice I ever got? ‘Keep calm and paddle on.’ It was from a goose. Don’t tell the ducks.
